title: US-001 AC3 ([oracle: file-assert git check-ignore -q on each path token of the …
body: US-001 AC3 ([oracle: file-assert git check-ignore -q on each path token of the edited bullet exits non-zero]) is structurally vacuous: line 901 contains zero path tokens, so the loop body never executes and the oracle passes with zero iterations. The intent (no gitignored path token in the bullet) is satisfied, but a zero-match sweep passing silently is the same self-nullifying shape the bullet at patterns.md:901 warns about. Consider asserting a non-zero token count before iterating.

title: Worth capturing as a bullet: the review/measurement shell is zsh, where `$c:t` …
body: Worth capturing as a bullet: the review/measurement shell is zsh, where `$c:t` and `$c:s` are path modifiers, so a loop written as `git show "$c:test/foo.ts"` silently expands to `<sha>est/foo.ts` and, with stderr redirected, yields an empty file and a bogus `grep -c` of 0 for every commit. This produced two wrong measurements during this review and is the unidentified cause of the 'for-loop pipeline gave inconsistent readings' note in the round-2 artifact. Per-commit sweeps should run under an explicit `bash -c`.

title: Per-clause scoping (US-002) now flags a `git diff main --quiet -- file.ts; test…
body: Per-clause scoping (US-002) now flags a `git diff main --quiet -- file.ts; test $? -eq 0` exit-code idiom because the `-eq 0` sits in a different clause from the `git diff main` token. This is the intended, spec-encoded behavior (and the rule already flags a bare `test $? -eq 0` on main), but oracle authors relying on the two-clause exit-code shape will now be flagged and must restructure into one clause or a same-clause derivation. Non-blocking; consider a patterns.md note for oracle authors.
